landmarks.name: Eiffel Tower
landmarks.summary: The Eiffel Tower is a lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. It is named after the engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built the tower from 1887 to 1889.

landmarks.name: Great Wall of China
landmarks.description: Series of fortifications in northern China
landmarks.summary: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications in China. They were built across the historical northern borders of ancient Chinese states and Imperial China as protection against various nomadic groups from the Eurasian Steppe. The first walls date to the 7th century BC; these were joined together in the Qin dynasty.

landmarks.name: Colosseum
landmarks.summary: The Colosseum is an elliptical amphitheatre in the centre of the city of Rome, Italy, just east of the Roman Forum. It is the largest ancient amphitheatre ever built, and is the largest standing amphitheatre in the world. Construction began under Emperor Vespasian in 72 and was completed in AD 80 under his successor and heir, Titus.

landmarks.name: Panama Canal
landmarks.summary: The Panama Canal is an artificial 82-kilometer (51-mile) waterway in Panama that connects the Caribbean Sea in the Atlantic Ocean with the Pacific Ocean. It cuts across the narrowest point of the Isthmus of Panama and is a conduit for maritime trade between the Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean.

landmarks.name: Louvre
landmarks.summary: The Louvre is a national art museum in Paris, France. It is located on the Right Bank of the Seine in the city's 1st arrondissement (district) and home to some of the most canonical works of Western art, including the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and Winged Victory.

landmarks.name: Machu Picchu
landmarks.summary: Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel located in the Eastern Cordillera of southern Peru on a mountain ridge at 2,430 meters (7,970 ft).

landmarks.name: Troy
landmarks.description: Ancient city in northwest Asia Minor
landmarks.summary: Troy or Ilion was an ancient city located in present-day Çanakkale, Turkey. It is best known as the setting for the Greek myth of the Trojan War. The modern-day archaeological site, also known as Hisarlık, is open to the public as a tourist destination, and was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1998.

landmarks.description: Building at the center of Masjid al-Haram
landmarks.summary: The Kaaba, also spelled Kaʽba, Kaʽbah or Kabah, sometimes referred to as al-Kaʽba al-Musharrafa, is a stone building at the center of Islam's most important mosque and holiest site, the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. It is considered by Muslims to be the Baytullah and determines the qibla for Muslims around the world.

landmarks.name: Dead Sea
landmarks.summary: The Dead Sea, also known by other names, is a landlocked salt lake bordered by Jordan to the east, the West Bank to the west and Israel to the southwest. It lies in the endorheic basin of the Jordan Rift Valley, and its main tributary is the Jordan River.

landmarks.name: Sagrada Família
landmarks.description: Basilica under construction since 1882 in Barcelona, Spain
landmarks.summary: Basílica i Temple Expiatori de la Sagrada Família, or simply Sagrada Família, is a Catholic Basilica under construction in the Eixample district of Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain. Designed by the Spanish architect Antoni Gaudí, it is the tallest church in the world.

landmarks.name: Angkor Wat
landmarks.summary: Angkor Wat is a Theravada Buddhist temple complex, originally built as a Vaishnava Hindu temple, in Siem Reap, Cambodia. It is the largest religious complex in the world.

landmarks.name: Valletta
landmarks.summary: Valletta, also known as Città Umilissima, is the capital city of Malta and one of its 68 council areas. Located between the Grand Harbour to the east and Marsamxett Harbour to the west, its population as of 2021 was 5,157. As Malta's capital city, it is a commercial centre for shopping, bars, dining, and café life.

landmarks.name: Babylon
landmarks.summary: Babylon was an ancient city located on the lower Euphrates river in southern Mesopotamia, within modern-day Hillah, Iraq, about 85 kilometres south of modern-day Baghdad. Babylon functioned as the main cultural and political centre of the Akkadian-speaking region of Babylonia.

landmarks.name: Empire State Building
landmarks.description: Office skyscraper in Manhattan, New York
landmarks.summary: The Empire State Building is a 102-story, supertall skyscraper in the Midtown South neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States. The building was designed in the Art Deco style by Shreve, Lamb & Harmon and constructed between 1930 and 1931. Its name is derived from "Empire State", the nickname of New York state.

landmarks.name: Stonehenge
landmarks.summary: Stonehenge is a prehistoric megalithic structure on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, England, two miles (3 km) west of Amesbury. 1 m) wide, and weighing around 25 tons, topped by connecting horizontal lintel stones which are held in place with mortise and tenon joints—a feature unique among contemporary monuments.

landmarks.summary: Lake Victoria is one of the African Great Lakes. landmarks.summary: The Aral Sea was an endorheic salt lake lying between Kazakhstan to its north and Uzbekistan to its south, which began shrinking in the 1950s and had largely dried up into desert by 2007. It was in the Aktobe and Kyzylorda regions of Kazakhstan and the Karakalpakstan autonomous region of Uzbekistan.

landmarks.description: Coral reef system in Queensland, Australia
landmarks.summary: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, composed of over 2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands stretching for over 2,300 kilometres (1,400 mi) over an area of approximately 344,400 square kilometres (133,000 mi2). The reef is located in the Coral Sea, off the coast of Queensland, Australia.

landmarks.summary: The Galápagos Islands are an archipelago of volcanic islands in the Eastern Pacific, located around the equator, 485 nautical miles west of the mainland of South America. They form the Galápagos Province of the Republic of Ecuador, with a population of slightly over 33,450 in 2020.

landmarks.name: Carthage
landmarks.summary: Carthage was an ancient city in northern Africa founded by the legendary Phoenician queen Dido on the eastern side of the Lake of Tunis in what is now Tunisia. Carthage was one of the most important trading hubs of the Ancient Mediterranean and one of the most affluent cities of the classical world.

landmarks.summary: Notre-Dame de Paris, often referred to simply as Notre-Dame, is a medieval Catholic cathedral and basilica on the Île de la Cité, in the 4th arrondissement of Paris, France. It is the cathedral church of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Paris.

landmarks.name: Petra
landmarks.description: Ancient rock-cut historical city in Jordan
landmarks.summary: Petra is an ancient city and archaeological site in southern Jordan. Famous for its rock-cut architecture and water conduit systems, Petra is also called the "Rose City" because of the colour of the sandstone from which it is carved. The city is one of the New 7 Wonders of the World and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

landmarks.summary: The Leaning Tower of Pisa, or simply the Tower of Pisa, is the campanile, or freestanding bell tower, of Pisa Cathedral. It is known for its nearly four-degree lean, the result of an unstable foundation. The tower is one of three structures in Pisa's Cathedral Square, which includes the cathedral and Pisa Baptistry.

landmarks.description: Former royal residence in Versailles, France
landmarks.summary: The Palace of Versailles is a château and historic monument in Versailles in the Yvelines department of France, southwest of Paris. It served as the principal residence of the French kings Louis XIV, Louis XV, and Louis XVI.

landmarks.name: Lake Tanganyika
landmarks.summary: Lake Tanganyika is an African Great Lake. It is the world's second-largest freshwater lake by volume and the second deepest, in both cases after Lake Baikal in Siberia. It is the world's longest freshwater lake. It is also the 6th largest lake by area.

landmarks.name: Timbuktu
landmarks.summary: Timbuktu is a city in Mali, situated 20 kilometres north of the Niger River. It is the capital of the Tombouctou Region, one of the 19 administrative regions of Mali, with a population of around eighty-four thousand people in the 2023 census.

landmarks.name: Forbidden City
landmarks.description: Imperial palace complex in Beijing, China
landmarks.summary: The Forbidden City is the imperial palace complex in the center of the Imperial City in Beijing, China. It was the residence of twenty-four Ming and Qing dynasty Emperors and was the center of political power in China from 1420 to 1924.

credit.author: Pixelflake

landmarks.name: Taipei 101
landmarks.summary: Taipei 101, formerly known as the Taipei World Financial Center, is a 508-meter, 101-story skyscraper in Taipei, Taiwan. It is owned by the Taipei Financial Center Corporation. It was officially classified as the world's tallest building from its opening on 31 December 2004 until it was surpassed by the Burj Khalifa in 2009.

landmarks.name: Lake Titicaca
landmarks.description: Large lake on the border of Peru and Bolivia
landmarks.summary: Lake Titicaca is a large lake in the Andes mountains on the border of Bolivia and Peru. It is often called the highest navigable lake in the world. It is often listed as a freshwater lake, though its waters are slightly brackish. Titicaca is the largest lake in South America, both in terms of the volume of water and surface area.

It is known for its large circular structures that contain large stone pillars – among the world's oldest known megaliths.

landmarks.description: Administrative headquarters of the British monarch
landmarks.summary: Buckingham Palace is the official residence and administrative headquarters of the monarch of the United Kingdom in London, England. Located in the City of Westminster, the palace is often at the centre of state occasions and royal hospitality. It has been a focal point for the British people at times of national rejoicing and mourning.

landmarks.name: Cologne Cathedral
landmarks.summary: Cologne Cathedral is a Catholic cathedral in Cologne, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is a renowned monument of German Catholicism and Gothic architecture and was declared a World Heritage Site in 1996.

It lies in the Gangdise Shan mountain range of the Transhimalaya, in the western part of the Tibetan Plateau. landmarks.name: Moai of Easter Island
landmarks.summary: Moai or moꞌai are monolithic human figures carved from stone by the Rapa Nui people, on Rapa Nui in eastern Polynesia between the years 1250 and 1500. landmarks.description: Waterfalls on the Iguazú River on the border of Argentina and Brazil
landmarks.summary: The Iguazú Falls or Iguaçu Falls are waterfalls of the Iguazu River on the border of the Argentine province of Misiones and the Brazilian state of Paraná. Together, they make up the largest waterfall system in the world. The falls divide the river into the upper and lower Iguazu.

landmarks.summary: St Paul's Cathedral, formally the Cathedral Church of St Paul in London, is an Anglican cathedral in London, England, the seat of the bishop of London. landmarks.summary: Mohenjo-daro is an archaeological site in the Larkana District of Sindh, Pakistan. Built c. 2500 BCE, it was one of the largest settlements of the ancient Indus Valley Civilisation, and one of the world's earliest major cities, contemporaneous with the civilisations of ancient Egypt, Mesopotamia, Minoa, and Norte Chico.

landmarks.name: Mount Sinai
landmarks.summary: Mount Sinai, also known as Jabal Musa, is a mountain on the Sinai Peninsula of Egypt. It is one of several locations claimed to be the biblical Mount Sinai, the place where, according to the sacred scriptures of the three major Abrahamic religions, the Hebrew prophet Moses received the Ten Commandments from God.

landmarks.description: Volcano and highest mountain in Spain

landmarks.name: Pyramids of Giza
landmarks.summary: The Giza pyramid complex in Egypt is home to the Great Pyramid, the pyramid of Khafre, and the pyramid of Menkaure, along with their associated pyramid complexes and the Great Sphinx. All were built during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom of ancient Egypt, between c. 2600 – c. 2500 BC.

landmarks.summary: The Sea of Galilee, also called Lake Tiberias, Genezareth Lake or Kinneret, is a freshwater lake in northeast Israel. It is the lowest freshwater lake on Earth and the second-lowest lake in the world, with its elevation fluctuating between 215 and 209 metres below sea level.

landmarks.name: Brandenburg Gate
landmarks.description: Triumphal arch and gate in Berlin, Germany
landmarks.summary: The Brandenburg Gate is an 18th-century neoclassical monument in Berlin, Germany. One of the best-known landmarks of the country, it was erected on the site of a former city gate that marked the start of the road from Berlin to Brandenburg an der Havel, the former capital of the Margraviate of Brandenburg.

landmarks.name: Palmyra
landmarks.summary: Palmyra is an ancient city in central Syria. Located in the eastern part of the Levant, archaeological finds around the site date back to the Neolithic period, and documents first mention the city in the early second millennium BC.

landmarks.name: United States Capitol
landmarks.description: Meeting place of the United States Congress
landmarks.summary: The United States Capitol, often called the Capitol or the Capitol Building, is the seat of the United States Congress, the legislative branch of the federal government. C. S. Capitol forms the origin point for the street-numbering system of the district as well as its four quadrants.

landmarks.name: Hoover Dam
landmarks.description: Dam in Nevada and Arizona, US
landmarks.summary: S. states of Nevada and Arizona. Constructed between 1931 and 1936, during the Great Depression, it was dedicated on September 30, 1935, by President Franklin D. Roosevelt. Its construction was the result of a massive effort involving thousands of workers, and cost over 96 lives.

landmarks.name: Statue of Unity
landmarks.description: Colossal statue of Vallabhbhai Patel in Gujarat, India
landmarks.summary: The Statue of Unity is the world's tallest statue, with a height of 182 metres, located in Narmada valley, near Kevadia in the state of Gujarat, India. It depicts Indian politician and independence activist Sardar Patel (1875–1950), who was the first deputy prime minister and home minister of independent India.

landmarks.name: Chrysler Building
landmarks.description: Office skyscraper in Manhattan, New York
landmarks.summary: The Chrysler Building is a 1,046-foot-tall (319 m), Art Deco-style supertall skyscraper in the East Midtown neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States. Located at the intersection of 42nd Street and Lexington Avenue, it is the tallest steel-framed brick building in the world.

landmarks.name: Nanga Parbat
landmarks.summary: Nanga Parbat, known in Shina as Diamer, is the ninth-highest mountain on Earth with its summit at 8,126 m (26,660 ft) above sea level.

landmarks.name: Angel Falls
landmarks.description: Tallest single drop waterfall in the world, Venezuela
landmarks.summary: Angel Falls is a waterfall in Venezuela. It is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, with a height of 979 metres (3,212 ft), and a plunge of 807 m (2,648 ft). The waterfall drops over the edge of the Auyán-tepui mountain in the Canaima National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Gran Sabana region of Bolívar State.

landmarks.name: Santorini
landmarks.description: Greek island in the Aegean Sea
landmarks.summary: Santorini, officially Thira or Thera, is a Greek island in the southern Aegean Sea, about 200 km (120 mi) southeast from the mainland. It is the largest island of a small, circular archipelago formed by the Santorini caldera.

landmarks.name: Milan Cathedral
landmarks.summary: Milan Cathedral, or Metropolitan Cathedral-Basilica of the Nativity of Saint Mary, is the cathedral church of Milan, Lombardy, Italy. Dedicated to the Nativity of St. Mary, it is the seat of the Archbishop of Milan, currently Archbishop Mario Delpini.

landmarks.name: Red Square
landmarks.summary: Red Square is one of the oldest and largest squares in Moscow, Russia. It is in Moscow's historic centre, along the eastern walls of the Kremlin. It is the city's most prominent landmark, with famous buildings such as Saint Basil's Cathedral, Lenin's Mausoleum, the State Historical Museum and the GUM department store.

landmarks.name: Lake Chad
landmarks.summary: Lake Chad is an endorheic freshwater lake located at the junction of four countries: Nigeria, Niger, Chad, and Cameroon, in western and central Africa, with a catchment area in excess of 1,000,000 km2 (390,000 sq mi). It is an important wetland ecosystem in West-Central Africa.

landmarks.name: Blue Mosque
landmarks.summary: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque, popularly known as the Blue Mosque, is an Ottoman-era historical imperial mosque located in Istanbul, Turkey. It was constructed between 1609 and 1617 during the rule of Ahmed I. It attracts a large number of tourists and is one of the most iconic and popular monuments of Ottoman architecture.

landmarks.name: Delphi
landmarks.description: Sacred site and oracle of Ancient Greece
landmarks.summary: Delphi, in legend previously called Pytho (Πυθώ), was an ancient sacred precinct in central Greece. It was the seat of Pythia, the high priestess role which was consulted as a major oracle for important decisions throughout the ancient classical world.

landmarks.description: Historical Mughal fort in Delhi, India
landmarks.summary: The Red Fort is a historic Mughal fort located in the Old Delhi area of Delhi, India. landmarks.description: U.S. national memorial in Washington, D.C.
landmarks.summary: , built to commemorate George Washington, a Founding Father of the United States and the nation's first president. Standing east of the Reflecting Pool and the Lincoln Memorial, the monument is made of bluestone gneiss for the foundation and of granite for the construction.

landmarks.name: Times Square
landmarks.description: Intersection and area in Manhattan, New York
landmarks.summary: Times Square is one of the world's busiest pedestrian intersections, tourist destinations, and entertainment hubs. It is formed by the junction of Broadway, Seventh Avenue, and 42nd Street in Midtown Manhattan, New York City.

landmarks.name: Abu Simbel
landmarks.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site in southern Egypt
landmarks.summary: Abu Simbel is a historic site comprising two massive rock-cut temples in the village of Abu Simbel, Aswan Governorate, Upper Egypt, near the border with Sudan. It is located on the western bank of Lake Nasser, about 230 km (140 mi) southwest of Aswan.

landmarks.name: Lake Como
landmarks.summary: Lake Como, also known as Lario, is a lake of glacial origin in Lombardy, Italy. It has an area of 146 km2 (56 sq mi), making it the third-largest lake in Italy, after Lake Garda and Lake Maggiore. At over 400 metres (1,300 ft) deep, it is one of the deepest lakes in Europe.

landmarks.summary: Fallingwater is a house museum in Stewart Township in the Laurel Highlands of southwestern Pennsylvania, United States. Designed by the architect Frank Lloyd Wright, it is built partly over a waterfall on the Bear Run stream. The three-story residence was developed as a weekend retreat for Edgar J.

landmarks.name: Giant's Causeway
landmarks.description: Interlocking basalt columns in Northern Ireland
landmarks.summary: The Giant's Causeway is an area of approximately 40,000 interlocking basalt columns, the result of an ancient volcanic fissure eruption, part of the North Atlantic Igneous Province active in the region during the Paleogene period.

landmarks.name: Nazca Lines
landmarks.description: Geoglyphs in the Nazca Desert, Peru
landmarks.summary: The Nazca lines are a group of geoglyphs made in the soil of the Nazca Desert in southern Peru. The area was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1994. The lines were created between 500 BC and 500 AD by people making depressions or shallow incisions in the desert floor, removing pebbles and leaving different-colored dirt exposed.

landmarks.name: Reichstag Building
landmarks.description: Seat of the federal parliament of Germany
landmarks.summary: The Reichstag is a historic legislative government building on Platz der Republik in Berlin that is the seat of the Bundestag parliament. It is also the meeting place of the Federal Convention, which elects the president of Germany.

landmarks.name: Florence Cathedral
landmarks.summary: Florence Cathedral, formally the Cathedral of Saint Mary of the Flower, is the cathedral of the Catholic Archdiocese of Florence in Florence, Italy.

landmarks.name: Kennedy Space Center
landmarks.summary: The John F. Kennedy Space Center, located on Merritt Island, Florida, is one of the ten field centers of NASA. Since 1968, KSC has been NASA's primary launch center of American spaceflight, research, and technology.

landmarks.summary: Mount Kosciuszko is the highest mountain of mainland Australia, at 2,228 metres (7,310 ft) above sea level.

landmarks.name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
landmarks.summary: The Cathedral of Vasily the Blessed, commonly known as Saint Basil's Cathedral, is a Russian Orthodox church on Red Square in the historic centre of Moscow. It is one of the most popular cultural symbols of Russia.

landmarks.name: Maldives
landmarks.summary: The Maldives, officially the Republic of Maldives, and historically known as the Maldive Islands, is an archipelagic country in South Asia, located in the Indian Ocean, near the southeastern boundary of the Arabian Sea. The Maldives is located southwest of India and Sri Lanka, about 750 kilometres from the Asian continent's mainland.

landmarks.name: Topkapı Palace
landmarks.summary: The Topkapı Palace or the Seraglio, is a large museum and library in the east of the Fatih district of Istanbul in Turkey. From the 1460s to the completion of Dolmabahçe Palace in 1853, it served as the administrative center of the Ottoman Empire, and was the main residence of its sultans.

credit.title: File:Bağdat Köşkü, or Kiosk of Baghdad, located in Topkapı Palace..jpg
credit.author: BWV784

landmarks.name: Trafalgar Square
landmarks.summary: Trafalgar Square is a public square in the City of Westminster in Central London. It was established in the early 19th century around the area known as Charing Cross.

landmarks.name: Arlington National Cemetery
landmarks.summary: Arlington National Cemetery is the largest cemetery in the United States National Cemetery System, one of two maintained by the United States Army. More than 400,000 people are buried in its 639 acres in Arlington County, Virginia.

credit.title: File:Arlington National Cemetery 2012.jpg
credit.author: Photo taken by IP Singh ( Ipsingh at en.wikipedia )

landmarks.name: Cape Horn
landmarks.description: Headland of the Tierra del Fuego archipelago in Chile
landmarks.summary: Cape Horn is the southernmost headland of the Tierra del Fuego archipelago of southern Chile, and is located on the small Hornos Island. Although not the most southerly point of South America, Cape Horn marks both the northern boundary of the Drake Passage and where the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans meet.

landmarks.name: Potala Palace
landmarks.summary: Potala Palace is a museum complex in Lhasa, the capital of the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. It was formerly the winter palace of the Dalai Lamas, and from 1649 until 1959 served as the Dalai Lamas' residence. The palace complex became a museum following the annexation of Tibet by the People's Republic of China.

landmarks.name: Alcatraz Island
landmarks.description: Island in San Francisco Bay, California, US
landmarks.summary: 25 miles offshore from San Francisco in San Francisco Bay, California, near the Golden Gate strait. The island was developed in the mid-19th century with facilities for a lighthouse, a military fortification, and a military prison. In 1934, the island was converted into a federal prison, Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary.

landmarks.name: Himeji Castle
landmarks.summary: Himeji Castle is a hilltop Japanese castle complex situated in Himeji, a city in Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan. The castle is regarded as the finest surviving example of prototypical Japanese castle architecture, comprising a network of 83 structures with advanced defensive systems from the feudal period.

landmarks.name: Winter Palace
landmarks.description: Former imperial palace in Saint Petersburg, Russia
landmarks.summary: The Winter Palace is a palace in Saint Petersburg that served as the official residence of the House of Romanov, the emperors of Russia, from 1732 to 1917. The palace and its precincts now house the Hermitage Museum. The floor area is 233,345 square metres. 2 hectares.

credit.title: File:Small Throne Room of the Winter Palace.jpg
credit.author: Balsamic Fan

landmarks.name: Knossos
landmarks.description: Archaeological site and Minoan palace complex in Heraklion, Crete
landmarks.summary: Knossos is an archaeological site and ancient urban centre in Crete, Greece. 1 mi) south of the city's historic centre. The site was occupied from the Neolithic period into the first millennium AD and became the largest and best-known centre of the Minoan civilisation.

landmarks.name: Qutb Minar
landmarks.description: Minaret in the Mehrauli area of Delhi, India
landmarks.summary: The Qutb Minar, also spelled Qutub Minar and Qutab Minar, is a minaret and victory tower, built during the Delhi sultanate, and comprising the Qutb complex, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Mehrauli, South Delhi, India.

landmarks.name: Abraj Al Bait
landmarks.description: Building complex in Makkah, Saudi Arabia Mecca region
landmarks.summary: The Clock Towers, formerly known as Abraj al-Bait, is a government-owned hotel complex with seven skyscraper hotels in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. These towers are part of the King Abdulaziz Endowment Project that aims to modernize the city in catering to its pilgrims.

landmarks.name: Lake Malawi
landmarks.summary: Lake Malawi, also known as Lake Nyasa in Tanzania and Lago Niassa in Mozambique, is an African Great Lake and the southernmost lake in the East African Rift system, located between Malawi, Mozambique and Tanzania.

landmarks.name: Chimborazo
landmarks.description: Volcano and highest mountain in Ecuador
landmarks.summary: Chimborazo is a stratovolcano in Ecuador and the Cordillera Occidental range of the Andes. Its last known eruption is believed to have occurred around AD 550.

landmarks.name: Great Zimbabwe
landmarks.description: Ruins of an ancient/medieval city in southeast Zimbabwe
landmarks.summary: Great Zimbabwe was a city in the south-eastern hills of the modern country of Zimbabwe, near Masvingo. It was settled by ancestral Shona people from around 1000 AD, and served as the capital of the Kingdom of Great Zimbabwe from the 13th century.

landmarks.name: Capri
landmarks.description: Island in the Tyrrhenian Sea, Italy
landmarks.summary: Capri is an island located in the Tyrrhenian Sea off the Sorrento Peninsula, on the south side of the Gulf of Naples in the Campania region of Italy. A resort destination since the time of the Roman Republic, it is known for its natural beauty, historic sites, and tourism industry. It has 13,451 inhabitants.

credit.title: File:Italie 2020 (49608950896).jpg
credit.author: Nicolas Buffler from Guilherand Granges, France

landmarks.name: The Shard
landmarks.summary: The Shard, also referred to as the Shard London Bridge and formerly London Bridge Tower, is a 95-storey mixed-use development supertall pyramid-shaped skyscraper, designed by the Italian architect Renzo Piano, in Southwark, London, that forms part of The Shard Quarter development.

credit.author: Richard Goldschmidt, www.piqtured.com
credit.credit: " The Shard inauguration ceremony light show " on Flickr

landmarks.name: Blenheim Palace
landmarks.summary: Blenheim Palace is a country house in Woodstock, Oxfordshire, England. It is the seat of the Dukes of Marlborough, and the birthplace of Sir Winston Churchill. Originally called Blenheim Castle, it has been known as Blenheim Palace since the 19th century.

credit.title: File:Blenheim Palace from the Water Terraces October 2016.jpg
credit.author: DeFacto

landmarks.name: Herculaneum
landmarks.description: Roman town destroyed by eruption of Mount Vesuvius
landmarks.summary: Herculaneum is an ancient Roman town located in the modern-day comune of Ercolano, Campania, Italy. Herculaneum was buried under a massive pyroclastic flow in the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD.

credit.title: File:Antigua ciudad de Herculano, Italia, 2023-03-27, DD 135-138 PAN.jpg
credit.author: Diego Delso

landmarks.name: Gjirokastër
landmarks.summary: Gjirokastër is a city in southern Albania and the seat of Gjirokastër County and Gjirokastër Municipality. It is located in a valley between the Gjerë mountains and the Drino, at 300 metres above sea level. Its old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

landmarks.name: Lake Garda
landmarks.summary: Lake Garda is the largest lake in Italy. It is a popular holiday location in northern Italy, between Brescia and Milan to the west, and Verona and Venice to the east. The lake cuts into the edge of the Italian Alps, particularly the Alpine sub-ranges of the Garda Mountains and the Brenta Group.

credit.title: File:La Rocca di Manerba del Garda con l'isola dei Conigli.jpg
credit.author: Photo by Guido Adler. Upload by Moroder

landmarks.name: Jaffa
landmarks.description: Ancient port and city in Tel Aviv, Israel
landmarks.summary: Jaffa, also called Japho, Joppa or Joppe in English, is an ancient Levantine port city which is part of Tel Aviv-Yafo, Israel, located in its southern part. The city sits atop a naturally elevated outcrop on the Mediterranean coastline.

landmarks.name: Tokyo Tower
landmarks.description: Communications and observation tower in Japan
landmarks.summary: Tokyo Tower , also known by its official name Japan Radio Tower is a communications and observation tower in the district of Shiba-koen in Minato, Tokyo, Japan, completed in 1958. 9 meters, it was the tallest tower in Japan until the construction of Tokyo Skytree in 2012.

credit.title: File:Tokyo Tower and Tokyo Sky Tree 2011 January.jpg
credit.author: Morio

landmarks.name: Baalbek
landmarks.summary: Baalbek is a city located east of the Litani River in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley, about 67 km (42 mi) northeast of Beirut. It is the capital of Baalbek-Hermel Governorate. In 1998, the city had a population of 82,608.

landmarks.name: Bondi Beach
landmarks.description: Suburb of Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
landmarks.summary: Bondi Beach is a beach and the surrounding suburb in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia. Bondi Beach is located 7 kilometres east of the Sydney central business district, in the local government area of Waverley Council, in the Eastern Suburbs. In the 2021 Australian census it had a population of 11,513 residents. Its postcode is 2026.

landmarks.name: Museo del Prado
landmarks.description: National art museum in Madrid, Spain
landmarks.summary: The Museo del Prado, officially known as Museo Nacional del Prado, is the main Spanish national art museum, located in central Madrid. It houses collections of European art, dating from the 12th century to the early 20th century, based on the former Spanish royal collection, and is the single best collection of Spanish art in the world.

landmarks.name: Hallstatt
landmarks.summary: Hallstatt is a small town in the Gmunden District of the Austrian state of Upper Austria. Situated between the southwestern shore of Hallstätter See and the steep slopes of the Dachstein massif, the town lies in the Salzkammergut region, on the national road linking Salzburg and Graz.

credit.title: File:Blue Hallstatt (204466021).jpeg
credit.author: Ioan Sendroiu

landmarks.name: Manneken Pis
landmarks.description: Brass sculpture and fountain in Brussels, Belgium
landmarks.summary: 9 in) bronze fountain sculpture in central Brussels, Belgium, depicting a puer mingens: a nude boy urinating into the fountain's basin. Though its existence is attested as early as the mid-15th century, Manneken Pis was redesigned by the Brabantine sculptor Jérôme Duquesnoy the Elder and put in place in 1619.

landmarks.name: Øresund Bridge
landmarks.description: Road and railway bridge connecting Sweden and Denmark
landmarks.summary: The Øresund Bridge or Öresund Bridge is a combined railway and motorway cable-stayed bridge across the Øresund strait between Denmark and Sweden. It is the third longest bridge in Europe and combines both roadway and railway in a single structure, consisting of international European route E20 and the Øresund Line respectively.

landmarks.name: Panthéon, Paris
landmarks.summary: The Panthéon is a monument in the 5th arrondissement of Paris, France. It stands in the Latin Quarter, on the Montagne Sainte-Geneviève, in the centre of the Place du Panthéon, which was named after it.

landmarks.name: Saint Catherine's Monastery
landmarks.summary: Saint Catherine's Monastery, officially the Sacred Autonomous Royal Monastery of Saint Catherine of the Holy and God-Trodden Mount Sinai, is a Christian monastery located in the Sinai Peninsula of Egypt.

credit.title: File:A full view of Saint Catherine's Monastery.jpg
credit.author: Dr. Ondřej Havelka (cestovatel)

landmarks.name: Ellora Caves
landmarks.description: Ancient cave temples in Maharashtra, India
landmarks.summary: The Ellora Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Aurangabad, India. It is one of the largest rock-cut cave complexes in the world, with artwork dating from AD 600–1000, including Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain caves.

credit.title: File:Kailasa Temple Cave 16 Hindu Cave Ellora Caves India - panoramio (4).jpg
credit.author: Hiroki Ogawa

landmarks.name: Wrangel Island
landmarks.description: Russian island in the Arctic Ocean
landmarks.summary: Wrangel Island is an island of the Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, Russia. It is the 92nd-largest island in the world and roughly the size of Crete. Located in the Arctic Ocean between the Chukchi Sea and East Siberian Sea, the island lies astride the 180th meridian.

landmarks.name: Sacré-Cœur
landmarks.description: Catholic basilica and landmark in Paris, France
landmarks.summary: The Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Montmartre, commonly known as Sacré-Cœur Basilica or simply Sacré-Cœur, is a Catholic church and minor basilica in Paris dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.

credit.author: OliveiraTP

landmarks.name: Ellis Island
landmarks.description: Island in New York Harbor in the US
landmarks.summary: S. states of New Jersey and New York. S. government, Ellis Island was the busiest immigrant inspection and processing station in the United States.

landmarks.name: Mosque–Cathedral of Córdoba
landmarks.description: Cathedral and former mosque in Córdoba, Spain
landmarks.summary: The Mosque–Cathedral of Córdoba is the cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Córdoba in the Spanish region of Andalusia. Officially called the Cathedral of Our Lady of the Assumption, it is dedicated to the Assumption of Mary.

landmarks.name: McMurdo Station
landmarks.summary: McMurdo Station is an American Antarctic research station on the southern tip of Ross Island. It is operated by the United States through the United States Antarctic Program (USAP), a branch of the National Science Foundation (NSF).

landmarks.name: Puncak Jaya
landmarks.description: Highest mountain in Indonesia and Oceania
landmarks.summary: Puncak Jaya or Carstensz Pyramid on the island of New Guinea, with an elevation of 4,884 m (16,024 ft), is the highest mountain peak of an island on Earth, and the highest peak in Indonesia and within Oceania. The mountain is located in the Sudirman Range of the highlands of Mimika Regency, Central Papua, Indonesia.

landmarks.name: Roman Forum
landmarks.description: Ancient Roman centre of Rome, Italy
landmarks.summary: The Roman Forum, also known by its Latin name Forum Romanum, is a rectangular forum (plaza) surrounded by the ruins of several important ancient government buildings at the centre of the city of Rome. Citizens of the ancient city referred to this space, originally a marketplace, as the Forum Magnum, or simply the Forum.

landmarks.name: Temple of Heaven
landmarks.description: Imperial complex of religious buildings in Beijing, China
landmarks.summary: The Temple of Heaven is a complex of imperial religious Confucian buildings situated in the southeastern part of central Beijing. The complex was visited by the Emperors of the Ming and then later restored by the Qing dynasties for annual ceremonies of prayer to Heaven for a good harvest and other seasonal rites.

landmarks.name: Tyre
landmarks.summary: Tyre is a city in Lebanon, and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. It was one of the earliest Phoenician metropolises and the legendary birthplace of Europa, her brothers Cadmus and Phoenix, and Carthage's founder Dido (Elissa).

landmarks.name: Mayon Volcano
landmarks.summary: Mayon, also known as Mount Mayon and Mayon Volcano, is an active stratovolcano in the province of Albay in Bicol, Philippines. A popular tourist destination, it is renowned for its "perfect cone" owing to its symmetric conical shape, and is regarded as sacred in Philippine mythology.

landmarks.name: Svalbard Global Seed Vault
landmarks.description: Globally accessible seed bank on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, Norway
landmarks.summary: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault is a secure backup facility for the Earth's crop diversity on the Norwegian island of Spitsbergen in the remote Arctic Svalbard archipelago. The Seed Vault provides long-term storage for duplicates of seeds from around the world, conserved in gene banks.

landmarks.name: Lumbini
landmarks.description: Historical city in Lumbini Province, Nepal
landmarks.summary: Lumbini is a Buddhist pilgrimage site in the Rupandehi District of Lumbini Province in Nepal. According to sacred texts and Buddhist commentaries, Queen Maya gave birth to Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, in Lumbini, c. 563 BCE. Lumbini is one of the four most sacred pilgrimage sites pivotal in the life of the Buddha.

credit.title: File:The World Peace Pagoda - Lumbini.jpg
credit.author: tearsxintherain
credit.credit: originally posted to Flickr as The World Peace Pagoda - Lumbini

landmarks.name: Shanghai Tower
landmarks.summary: The Shanghai Tower is a 128-story, 632-meter-tall (2,073-foot) megatall skyscraper located in Lujiazui, Pudong, Shanghai. It is currently the tallest building in China, the world's third-tallest building by height to architectural top, and the world's second-tallest building by height to highest occupied floor.

credit.author: Chatterjee.kaushik

landmarks.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
landmarks.description: Bridge across Sydney Harbour in Australia
landmarks.summary: The Sydney Harbour Bridge is a steel through arch bridge in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia, spanning Sydney Harbour from the central business district (CBD) to the North Shore. The view of the bridge, the harbour, and the nearby Sydney Opera House is widely regarded as an iconic image of Sydney, and of Australia itself.

landmarks.name: Umayyad Mosque
landmarks.summary: The Umayyad Mosque, also known as the Great Mosque of Damascus, located in the old city of Damascus, the capital of Syria, is one of the largest and oldest mosques in the world. It is considered to be the oldest mosque still in use in its original form.

credit.title: File:Minaret of the Bride, Umayyad Mosque 01.jpg
credit.author: Bernard Gagnon

landmarks.name: Mount Pinatubo
landmarks.summary: Mount Pinatubo is an active stratovolcano in the Zambales Mountains in Luzon in the Philippines. Located on the tripoint of Zambales, Tarlac and Pampanga provinces, most people were unaware of its eruptive history before the pre-eruption volcanic activity in early 1991.

landmarks.name: Schönbrunn Palace
landmarks.summary: Schönbrunn Palace was the main summer residence of the Habsburg rulers, located in Hietzing, the 13th district of Vienna. The name Schönbrunn has its roots in an artesian well from which water was consumed by the court.

landmarks.name: Sigiriya
landmarks.description: Ancient rock fortress near Dambulla, Sri Lanka
landmarks.summary: Sigiriya or Sinhagiri is an ancient rock fortress located in the northern Matale District near the town of Dambulla in the Central Province, Sri Lanka. It is a site of historical and archaeological significance that is dominated by a massive column of granite approximately 180 m (590 ft) high.

credit.title: File:Sigiriya (141688197).jpeg
credit.author: Wrobell
credit.credit: Imported from 500px ( archived version ) by the Archive Team . ( detail page )

landmarks.name: Sundarbans
landmarks.description: Mangrove forest in the Bay of Bengal
landmarks.summary: Sundarbans is a mangrove forest area in the Ganges Delta formed by the confluence of the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna Rivers in the Bay of Bengal. It spans the area from the Hooghly River in India's state of West Bengal to the Baleswar River in Bangladesh's Khulna Division.

credit.title: File:Sundarbans a few months after cyclone sidr.jpg
credit.author: joiseyshowaa

landmarks.name: Agra Fort
landmarks.summary: Agra Fort, also known as the Red Fort of Agra (Lal-Qila) or Qila-i-Akbari, is an historic fort in the city of Agra in Uttar Pradesh, India. A brick fortification on the site, noted as early as 1080 and later known as Badalgarh, was extensively rebuilt in red sandstone by the Mughal emperor Akbar from 1565 to 1573.

credit.title: File:Exterior, full views of Jahangiri Mahal (Agra Fort).jpg
credit.author: Dudva

credit.title: File:Angoori Bagh at Agra Fort - in front of Shahjahan Mahal 05.JPG
credit.author: g.kaustav

credit.title: File:Taj and jamuna river from Agra Fort.jpg

landmarks.name: Darvaza Gas Crater
landmarks.description: Burning natural gas field in Turkmenistan
landmarks.summary: The Darvaza gas crater, also known as the Door to Hell or Gates of Hell, and known officially as the Shining of Karakum, is a burning natural gas field collapsed into a cavern near Darvaza, Turkmenistan. Hundreds of natural gas fires illuminate the floor and rim of the crater. The gas crater has been burning since 1971.

credit.title: File:Darvaza gas crater, Jähennem derwezesi, Door to Hell, Gates of Hell, Derweze, Turkmenistan.jpg
credit.author: Benjamin Goetzinger

credit.title: File:Darvaza Gas Crater (42435083112).jpg
credit.author: John Pavelka from Austin, TX, USA

landmarks.name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
landmarks.description: Modern and contemporary art museum in Bilbao, Spain
landmarks.summary: The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao is a museum of modern and contemporary art in Bilbao, Biscay, Spain. It is one of several museums affiliated to the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation and features permanent and visiting exhibits of works by Spanish and international artists.

credit.title: File:GuggenheimBilbao.jpg
credit.author: E. Goergen
credit.credit: own work by the original uploader

landmarks.name: Cinque Terre
landmarks.description: Rugged portion of coast on the Italian Riviera, Liguria
landmarks.summary: The Cinque Terre is a coastal area within Liguria, in the northwest of Italy. It lies in the west of La Spezia Province, and comprises five villages: Monterosso al Mare, Vernazza, Corniglia, Manarola and Riomaggiore.

landmarks.name: Pergamon
landmarks.summary: Pergamon or Pergamum, also referred to by its modern Greek form Pergamos (Πέργαμος), was a rich and powerful ancient Greek city in Aeolis. It is located 26 kilometres (16 mi) from the modern coastline of the Aegean Sea on a promontory on the north side of the river Caicus and northwest of the modern city of Bergama, Turkey.

landmarks.name: Canterbury Cathedral
landmarks.summary: Canterbury Cathedral is the cathedral of the archbishop of Canterbury, the spiritual leader of the Church of England and symbolic leader of the worldwide Anglican Communion. Located in Canterbury, Kent, it is on the site of one of the oldest Christian structures in England and forms part of a World Heritage Site.

credit.author: Tony Hisgett from Birmingham, UK

landmarks.name: Masada
landmarks.summary: Masada is a mountain-top fortress complex in the Judaean Desert, overlooking the western shore of the Dead Sea in southeastern Israel. The fort, built in the first century BC, was constructed atop a natural plateau rising over 400 m (1,300 ft) above the surrounding terrain, 20 km (12 mi) east of modern Arad.

landmarks.name: Mount Erebus
landmarks.summary: Mount Erebus is the southernmost active volcano on Earth, located on Ross Island in the Ross Dependency in Antarctica. With a summit elevation of 3,792 metres (12,441 ft), it is the second most prominent mountain in Antarctica and the second-highest volcano in Antarctica.

landmarks.name: Prague Castle
landmarks.description: Historic building in the Czech Republic
landmarks.summary: Prague Castle is a castle complex in Prague, Czech Republic serving as the official residence and workplace of the president of the Czech Republic. Built in the 9th century, the castle has long served as the seat of power for kings of Bohemia, Holy Roman emperors, and presidents of Czechoslovakia.

landmarks.name: Amalfi Coast
landmarks.description: Coastal area in the Campania region, Italy
landmarks.summary: The Amalfi Coast is a stretch of coastline overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea and the Gulf of Salerno. It is located in the Province of Salerno, in the Campania region of southern Italy, south of the Sorrentine Peninsula and north of the Cilentan Coast.

credit.title: File:Amalfi Coast, Italy from a tour boat.jpg
credit.author: Peter K Burian

landmarks.name: Byblos
landmarks.summary: Byblos, also known as Jbail, Jebeil, Jbeil or Jubayl, is an ancient city in the Keserwan-Jbeil Governorate of Lebanon. The area is believed to have been first settled between 8800 and 7000 BC and continuously inhabited since 5000 BC.

credit.title: File:Byblos-109933.jpg
credit.author: Véronique Dauge

landmarks.name: Devils Tower
landmarks.description: Flat-topped volcanic plug in Wyoming, US
landmarks.summary: Devils Tower is a laccolithic butte, composed of igneous rock in the Bear Lodge Ranger District of the Black Hills, near Hulett and Sundance in Crook County, northeastern Wyoming, above the Belle Fourche River. It rises 1,267 feet (386 m) above the river, standing 867 ft (264 m) from summit to base.

credit.author: James St. John

credit.author: Anthony Maw

landmarks.name: Merv
landmarks.description: Ancient major city in Central Asia
landmarks.summary: Merv, also called the Merve Oasis, was a major Iranian city in Central Asia, located on the historical Silk Road, near today's Mary, Turkmenistan. Human settlements on the site of Merv existed from the 3rd millennium BC until the 18th century AD. It changed hands repeatedly throughout history.

credit.title: File:Mervturkmenistan.jpg
credit.author: Mark and Delwen

landmarks.name: Crater Lake
landmarks.description: Caldera lake in Oregon, United States
landmarks.summary: Crater Lake is a volcanic crater lake in south-central Oregon in the Western United States. It is the main feature of Crater Lake National Park and is a tourist attraction known for its deep blue color and water clarity.

credit.title: File:Crater Lake National Park - HCP - October 13, 2022 - 031.jpg
credit.author: Vulturesong

landmarks.name: Edinburgh Castle
landmarks.summary: Edinburgh Castle is a historic castle in Edinburgh, Scotland. It stands on Castle Rock, which has been occupied by humans since at least the Iron Age. There has been a royal castle on the rock since the reign of Malcolm III in the 11th century, and the castle continued to be a royal residence until 1633.

credit.title: File:Edinburgh Castle from Princes Street Gardens (1).jpg
credit.author: Nilfanion

landmarks.name: Flatiron Building
landmarks.summary: 6 m) steel-framed triangular building at 175 Fifth Avenue in the Flatiron District neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City, New York, US. Designed by Daniel Burnham and Frederick P. Dinkelberg, it opened in 1902.

landmarks.name: Khyber Pass
landmarks.description: Mountain pass in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
landmarks.summary: The Khyber Pass is a mountain pass in the Khyber District of the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, along the international border with Afghanistan. It connects the town of Landi Kotal to the Valley of Peshawar at Jamrud by traversing part of the White Mountains.

landmarks.name: Konark Sun Temple
landmarks.description: 13th-century UNESCO world heritage site in Odisha, India
landmarks.summary: Konark Sun Temple is a 13th-century CE Hindu Sun temple at Konark about 35 kilometres (22 mi) northeast from Puri city on the coastline in Puri district, Odisha, India. The temple is attributed to king Narasingha Deva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty about 1250 CE.

credit.author: Jayantanth

credit.author: Subhrajyoti07

landmarks.name: Les Invalides
landmarks.summary: The Hôtel des Invalides, commonly called Les Invalides, is a complex of buildings in the 7th arrondissement of Paris, France, containing museums and monuments, all relating to the military history of France, as well as a hospital and an old soldiers' retirement home, the building's original purpose.

credit.author: Thesupermat

credit.author: EduardoVieira88

credit.author: Thesupermat

landmarks.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
landmarks.summary: Castel Sant'Angelo, also known as Mausoleum of Hadrian, is a towering rotunda in Parco Adriano, Rome, Italy. It was initially commissioned by the Roman Emperor Hadrian as a mausoleum for himself and his family. The popes later used the building as a fortress and castle dedicated to Saint Michael the Archangel, and it is now a museum.

credit.title: File:Castel Sant'Angelo from Southeast, Rome, Italy.jpg
credit.author: Julian Lupyan

landmarks.name: Oymyakon
landmarks.summary: Oymyakon is a rural locality in Oymyakonsky District of the Sakha Republic, Russia, located in the Yana-Oymyakon Highlands, along the Indigirka River, 30 km (19 mi) northwest of Tomtor on the Kolyma Highway. Oymyakon is currently the coldest permanently inhabited human settlement on Earth.

landmarks.name: Shaolin Monastery
landmarks.description: Chan Buddhist temple in Dengfeng, China
landmarks.summary: Shaolin Monastery, also known as Shaolin Temple, is a Mahayana Buddhist monastic institution associated with the development of Chan Buddhism and Shaolin kung fu. It is located at the foot of Wuru Peak of the Mount Song mountain range in Dengfeng, Zhengzhou prefecture, in Henan, China.

credit.title: File:Shaolin Temple Maitreya Pagoda, Northern Song, 1087 AD (10200018863).jpg
credit.author: Gary Todd from Xinzheng, China
credit.credit: Shaolin Temple: Maitreya Pagoda, Northern Song, 1087 AD

landmarks.name: Kiyomizu-dera
landmarks.summary: Kiyomizu-dera is a Buddhist temple located in eastern Kyoto, Japan. It belongs to the Kita-Hosso sect of Japanese Buddhism and its honzon is a hibutsu statue of Jūichimen Kannon. The temple's full name is Otowa-san Kiyomizu-dera. The temple is the 16th stop on the Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage route.

credit.title: File:West gate (Sai-mon) on the Kiyomizu-dera temple complex Kyoto Japan by Don Ramey Logan.jpg
credit.author: Don Ramey Logan

landmarks.name: Mount Logan
landmarks.summary: Mount Logan is the highest mountain in Canada, and the second-highest peak in North America after Denali. The mountain was named after Sir William Edmond Logan, a Canadian geologist and founder of the Geological Survey of Canada (GSC).

credit.title: File:Mount Logan Knife ridge, east ridge by Christian Stangl (flickr).jpg
credit.author: Christian Stangl

credit.title: File:Mountain and footprints.JPG
credit.author: The original uploader was Isteffen at English Wikipedia .

landmarks.name: Issyk-Kul
landmarks.summary: Issyk-Kul or Ysyk-Köl is an endorheic saline lake in the western Tian Shan mountains in eastern Kyrgyzstan—just south of a dividing range separating Kyrgyzstan from Kazakhstan. It is the eighth-deepest lake in the world, the eleventh-largest lake in the world by volume, and the second-largest saline lake.

landmarks.name: Ha Long Bay
landmarks.summary: Hạ Long Bay or Halong Bay is a bay located in Northeastern Vietnam, administered by the city of Quảng Ninh. The name Hạ Long means "descending dragon". It features thousands of limestone karsts and islets in various shapes and sizes, for which it is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a popular travel destination.

credit.title: File:Halong Bay, Rock formations in fog.jpg
credit.author: Vyacheslav Argenberg

landmarks.name: Mount Kenya
landmarks.summary: Mount Kenya is the second highest mountain in Africa and the namesake of the country Kenya. 5 kilometres south of the equator, the mountain's highest peaks are Batian, Nelion, and Point Lenana.

credit.title: File:Pt Thomson Batian Nelion Mt Kenya.JPG
File:Batian Nelion and pt Slade in the foreground Mt Kenya.JPG
credit.author: User:Chris 73

landmarks.name: Mount of Olives
landmarks.summary: The Mount of Olives or Mount Olivet is a mountain ridge in East Jerusalem, east of and adjacent to Jerusalem's Old City. It is named for the olive groves that once covered its slopes. The southern part of the mount was the Silwan necropolis, attributed to the elite of the ancient Kingdom of Judah.

credit.author: Hagai Agmon-Snir حچاي اچمون-سنير חגי אגמון-שניר

landmarks.name: Vinson Massif
landmarks.summary: Vinson Massif is a large mountain massif in Antarctica that is 21 km (13 mi) long and 13 km (8 mi) wide and lies within the Sentinel Range of the Ellsworth Mountains. It overlooks the Ronne Ice Shelf near the base of the Antarctic Peninsula. The massif is located about 1,200 kilometers (750 mi) from the South Pole. S. Navy aircraft.

landmarks.name: Mount Damavand
landmarks.summary: Mount Damavand is a dormant stratovolcano in Iran. It is the highest peak in Iran and Western Asia, the highest volcano in Asia, and the third highest volcano in the Eastern Hemisphere, at an elevation of 5,610 metres (18,410 ft). Damāvand has a special place in Persian mythology and folklore.

credit.title: File:Damavand mount in water,Lar,Tehran کوه دماوند درون آب،سیاپلاس لار - panoramio.jpg
credit.author: Mahdi Kalhor

landmarks.name: Lake Toba
landmarks.description: Volcanic lake located in North Sumatra Province, Indonesia
landmarks.summary: Lake Toba is a large natural lake in North Sumatra and Indonesia. The lake is the massive caldera of the Toba supervolcano. 1°E. The lake is about 100 kilometres long, 30 kilometres (19 mi) wide, and up to 505 metres (1,657 ft) deep. It is the largest lake in Indonesia and the largest volcanic lake in the world.

credit.title: File:Lake Toba and the surrounding hills.jpg
credit.author: Bisajunisa

landmarks.name: Tikal
landmarks.description: Ruin of ancient Maya city in Guatemala
landmarks.summary: Tikal is the ruin of an ancient city, which was likely to have been called Yax Mutal, found in a rainforest in Guatemala.

landmarks.name: L'Anse aux Meadows
landmarks.description: Norse archaeological site in Newfoundland, Canada
landmarks.summary: L'Anse aux Meadows is an archaeological site, first excavated in the 1960s, of a Norse settlement dating to approximately 1000 CE. The site is located near St. Anthony on the northernmost tip of the island of Newfoundland in the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador.

credit.title: File:Authentic Viking recreation.jpg
credit.author: Dylan Kereluk from White Rock, Canada

credit.title: File:L'Anse aux Meadows, main area inside long house.jpg

landmarks.name: Cyrene
landmarks.description: Ancient Greek and Roman city near present-day Shahhat, Libya
landmarks.summary: Cyrene, also sometimes anglicized as Kyrene, was an ancient Greek colony and Roman city near present-day Shahhat in northeastern Libya in North Africa. It was part of the Pentapolis, an important group of five cities in the region, and gave the area its classical and early modern name Cyrenaica.

credit.title: File:Jabal Akhdar near Cyrene Eastern Libya.jpg
credit.author: Abdul-Jawad Elhusuni (عبدالجواد الحسوني)

landmarks.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial
landmarks.description: Preserved ruins of the atomic bombing of Hiroshima, Japan
landmarks.summary: The Hiroshima Peace Memorial , originally the Hiroshima Prefectural Industrial Promotion Hall, and now commonly called the Genbaku Dome, Atomic Bomb Dome or A-Bomb Dome , is part of Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park in Hiroshima, Japan, and was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996.

landmarks.name: Karnak
landmarks.summary: The Karnak Temple Complex, commonly known as Karnak, comprises a vast mix of temples, pylons, chapels, and other buildings near Luxor, Egypt. Construction at the complex began during the reign of Senusret I in the Middle Kingdom and continued into the Ptolemaic Kingdom, although most of the extant buildings date from the New Kingdom.

credit.title: File:Templo de Karnak, Luxor, Egipto, 2022-04-03, DD 156.jpg
credit.author: Diego Delso

landmarks.name: Meteora
landmarks.description: Rock formations and monasteries in Thessaly, Greece
landmarks.summary: Meteora is a rock formation in the regional unit of Trikala, in Thessaly, in northwestern Greece, hosting one of the most prominent complexes of Eastern Orthodox monasteries, viewed locally as second in importance only to Mount Athos. Their height is more than 20 metres (66 ft).

credit.title: File:Monastery of St. Stephen at Meteora by Joy of Museums.jpg
credit.author: Joyofmuseums

landmarks.name: Sphere
landmarks.description: Entertainment venue in the Las Vegas Valley, United States
landmarks.summary: Sphere is a music and entertainment arena in Paradise, Nevada, United States, east of the Las Vegas Strip. Designed by Populous, the project was announced by the Madison Square Garden Company in 2018, known then as the MSG Sphere.

credit.title: File:MSG Sphere at The Venetian under construction, Sep 2022.jpg

landmarks.name: Cave of the Patriarchs
landmarks.summary: The Cave of the Patriarchs or Tomb of the Patriarchs, known to Jews by its Biblical name Cave of Machpelah and to Muslims as the Ibrahami Mosque, or Sanctuary of Ibrahim, is a series of caves situated in the heart of the Old City of Hebron in the West Bank, 30 kilometres (19 mi) south of Jerusalem.

landmarks.name: Christmas Island
landmarks.summary: Christmas Island, officially the Territory of Christmas Island, is an Australian external territory in the Indian Ocean comprising the island of the same name. It is about 350 kilometres south of Java and Sumatra and about 1,550 km north-west of the closest point on the Australian mainland.

landmarks.name: Ryugyong Hotel
landmarks.description: Unfinished skyscraper in Pyongyang, North Korea
landmarks.summary: The Ryugyong Hotel, sometimes spelled as Yu-Kyung Hotel, is a 330 m (1,080 ft) tall unfinished pyramid-shaped skyscraper in Pyongyang, North Korea. Its name is also one of the historical names for Pyongyang. The building has been planned as a mixed-use development, which would include a hotel.

landmarks.name: Derinkuyu Underground City
landmarks.summary: Derinkuyu, also known as Malakopi, is an ancient multi-level underground city near the modern town of Derinkuyu in Nevşehir Province, Turkey, extending to a depth of approximately 85 metres (280 ft). It is large enough to have housed as many as 20,000 people together with their livestock and food stores.

landmarks.name: Hawa Mahal
landmarks.summary: The Hawa Mahal is a palace in the city of Jaipur, Rajasthan, India. Built from red and pink sandstone, it is on the edge of the City Palace, Jaipur, and extends to the Zenana, or women's chambers.

landmarks.name: Lincoln Memorial
landmarks.summary: S. C. The memorial is built in a neoclassical style in the form of a classical temple. The memorial's architect was Henry Bacon. In 1920, Daniel Chester French designed the large interior Abraham Lincoln statue, which was carved in marble by the Piccirilli brothers.

landmarks.name: Lofoten
landmarks.description: Archipelago and traditional district in Nordland, Norway
landmarks.summary: Lofoten is an archipelago and a traditional district in the county of Nordland, Norway. Lofoten has distinctive scenery with dramatic mountains and peaks, open sea and sheltered bays, beaches, and untouched lands.

credit.author: Ximonic (Simo Räsänen)

landmarks.name: Macquarie Island
landmarks.summary: Macquarie Island is a subantarctic island in the south-western Pacific Ocean, about halfway between Tasmania and Antarctica. It has been governed as a part of Tasmania, Australia, since 1880. It became a Tasmanian State Reserve in 1978 and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

landmarks.name: Monument Valley
landmarks.description: Region of the Colorado Plateau, US
landmarks.summary: Monument Valley is a region of the Colorado Plateau characterized by a cluster of sandstone buttes, with the largest reaching 1,000 ft (300 m) above the valley floor. The most famous butte formations are located in northeastern Arizona along the Utah–Arizona state line.

credit.title: File:Forrest Gump Point Monument Valley November 2018 001.jpg
credit.author: King of Hearts

landmarks.name: St Mark's Basilica
landmarks.summary: The Patriarchal Cathedral Basilica of Saint Mark, commonly known as St Mark's Basilica, is the cathedral church of the Patriarchate of Venice; it became the episcopal seat of the Patriarch of Venice in 1807, replacing the earlier cathedral of San Pietro di Castello.

credit.author: Zairon

landmarks.description: Mountain overlooking Cape Town, South Africa
landmarks.summary: Table Mountain is a flat-topped mountain forming a prominent landmark overlooking the city of Cape Town in South Africa.

credit.author: Danie van der Merwe from Cape Town, South Africa
credit.credit: View of Table Mountain from Bloubergstrand

landmarks.name: Taxila
landmarks.summary: Taxila, historically known as Takṣaśilā, is a city and a World Heritage Site in the Rawalpindi District of Punjab, Pakistan. Founded around c. 1000 BC, it is one of the oldest cities in Asia, and has a population of over 136,900 as of 2023.

landmarks.name: Gateway Arch
landmarks.description: US National Historic Landmark in St. Louis, Missouri
landmarks.summary: The Gateway Arch is a 630-foot-tall (192 m) monument in St. Louis, Missouri, United States. Clad in stainless steel and built in the form of a weighted catenary arch, it is the world's tallest arch and Missouri's tallest accessible structure. Some sources consider it the tallest human-made monument in the Western Hemisphere.

landmarks.name: Krak des Chevaliers
landmarks.summary: Krak des Chevaliers is a medieval castle in Syria and one of the most important preserved medieval castles in the world. The site was first inhabited in the 11th century by Kurdish troops garrisoned there by the Mirdasids. In 1142 it was given by Raymond II, Count of Tripoli, to the order of the Knights Hospitaller.

landmarks.name: Sainte-Chapelle
landmarks.description: French royal chapel in Paris, France
landmarks.summary: The Sainte-Chapelle is a royal chapel located on the Île de la Cité in the middle of the River Seine in Paris. It was part of the medieval Palais de la Cité, the main residence of the Kings of France until the 14th century.

landmarks.name: Palais Garnier
landmarks.summary: The Palais Garnier, also known as Opéra Garnier, is a historic 1,979-seat opera house at the Place de l'Opéra in the 9th arrondissement of Paris, France. It was built for the Paris Opera from 1861 to 1875 at the behest of Emperor Napoleon III.

landmarks.name: Hashima Island
landmarks.summary: Hashima Island , commonly called Gunkanjima , is an abandoned island about 15 kilometres from the centre of Nagasaki, Japan. It is one of 505 uninhabited islands in Nagasaki Prefecture. The island's most notable features are its abandoned concrete buildings, undisturbed except by nature, and the surrounding seawall.

credit.author: NevinThompson

landmarks.name: Hampi
landmarks.description: Ancient and medieval monuments, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Karnataka, India
landmarks.summary: Hampi or Hampe, also referred to as the Group of Monuments at Hampi, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in the town of Hampi in Vijayanagara district, east-central Karnataka, India. Hampi predates the Vijayanagara Empire; it is mentioned in the Ramayana and the Puranas of Hinduism as Pampa Devi Tirtha Kshetra.

landmarks.name: Malbork Castle
landmarks.summary: The Castle of the Teutonic Order in Malbork, commonly known as Malbork Castle, is a Brick Gothic castle complex located in the town of Malbork, Poland, built in the 13th and significantly expanded in the 14th century. It is the largest castle in the world measured by land area and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

landmarks.name: Salar de Uyuni
landmarks.summary: Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat in the world, with an area of approximately 10,582 square kilometres (4,086 mi2). It is situated in southwestern Bolivia, within the Daniel Campos Province of the Potosí Department, near the crest of the Andes Mountains, at an elevation of 3,656 m (11,995 ft) above sea level.

landmarks.name: Tristan da Cunha
landmarks.description: Group of islands in the South Atlantic
landmarks.summary: Tristan da Cunha, colloquially known as Tristan, is a remote group of volcanic islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. It is one of three constituent parts of the British Overseas Territory of Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha, with its own constitution.

landmarks.name: St. Stephen's Cathedral, Vienna
landmarks.summary: St. Stephen's Cathedral is a Roman Catholic church in Vienna, Austria, and the mother church of the Archdiocese of Vienna. It is the seat of the Archbishop of Vienna, Josef Grünwidl.

landmarks.name: Drakensberg
landmarks.summary: The Drakensberg is the eastern portion of the Great Escarpment, which encloses the central Southern African plateau. The Great Escarpment reaches its greatest elevation – 2,000 to 3,482 metres within the border region of South Africa and Lesotho.

landmarks.name: Richat Structure
landmarks.description: Circular geological feature in the Sahara desert
landmarks.summary: The Richat Structure, or Guelb er Richât, often called the Eye of Africa is a prominent circular geological feature at the northwestern edge of the Taoudeni Basin, on the Adrar Plateau of the Sahara. It is located near Ouadane in the Adrar Region of Mauritania.

landmarks.name: Rub' al Khali
landmarks.summary: The Rub' al Khali is a desert encompassing most of the southern third of the Arabian Peninsula. The desert covers some 650,000 km2 (250,000 sq mi), including parts of Saudi Arabia, Oman, the United Arab Emirates, and Yemen. It is part of the larger Arabian Desert.

landmarks.name: Golestan Palace
landmarks.description: Former official royal Qajar complex in Tehran, Iran
landmarks.summary: The Golestan Palace is the former official royal Qajar complex in Tehran, Iran.

landmarks.summary: The Hollywood Sign is an American landmark and cultural icon overlooking Hollywood, Los Angeles. Originally the Hollywoodland Sign, it is on Mount Lee, above Beachwood Canyon in the Santa Monica Mountains. 2 m) long. Due to increasing recognition, the sign was left up; the last four letters "LAND" were removed in 1949.

landmarks.name: Aoraki / Mount Cook
landmarks.summary: Aoraki / Mount Cook is the highest mountain in New Zealand. Its height, as of 2014, is listed as 3,724 metres. It is situated in the Southern Alps, the mountain range that runs the length of the South Island. A popular tourist destination, it is also a favourite challenge for mountaineers.

credit.author: David Wipf

landmarks.name: Biltmore Estate
landmarks.description: Historic house in North Carolina, US
landmarks.summary: Biltmore Estate is a historic house museum and tourist attraction in Asheville, North Carolina, United States. The main residence is the Biltmore House, a Châteauesque-style mansion built for George Washington Vanderbilt II between 1889 and 1895. 8 m2) of floor space and 135,280 sq ft (12,568 m2) of living area.

landmarks.name: Prambanan
landmarks.description: 9th-century Hindu temple compound near Yogyakarta, Indonesia
landmarks.summary: Prambanan is a 9th-century Hindu temple compound in the Special Region of Yogyakarta, in southern Java, Indonesia, dedicated to the Trimūrti, the expression of God as the Creator (Brahma), the Preserver (Vishnu), and the Destroyer (Shiva).

landmarks.name: Bran Castle
landmarks.summary: Bran Castle is a castle in Bran, 25 kilometres (16 mi) southwest of Brașov. The castle was built by Saxons in 1377 who were given the privilege by Louis I of Hungary. It is a national monument and landmark in Transylvania. The fortress is on the Transylvanian side of the historical border with Wallachia, on road DN73.

landmarks.name: Church of the Nativity
landmarks.summary: The Church of the Nativity, or Basilica of the Nativity, is a basilica located in Bethlehem, West Bank, Palestine. The grotto holds a prominent religious significance to Christians of various denominations as the birthplace of Jesus.

landmarks.name: Itsukushima Shrine
landmarks.description: Shinto shrine in Hiroshima Prefecture, Japan
landmarks.summary: Itsukushima Shrine is a Shinto shrine on the island of Itsukushima, best known for its "floating" torii. It is in the city of Hatsukaichi, in Hiroshima Prefecture in Japan, accessible from the mainland by ferry at Miyajimaguchi Station.

landmarks.name: Coober Pedy
landmarks.summary: Coober Pedy is a town in northern South Australia, 846 km (526 mi) from Adelaide via the Stuart Highway. The town is sometimes referred to as the "opal capital of the world" because of the quantity of precious opals mined there.

credit.author: eyeintim
credit.credit: Outback Trip - Coober Pedy Welcome Sign

landmarks.name: India Gate
landmarks.description: War memorial arch in New Delhi, India
landmarks.summary: The India Gate is a war memorial arch that’s located near the Rajpath on the eastern edge of the "ceremonial axis" of New Delhi, India.

landmarks.name: Pantanal
landmarks.description: Tropical wetland in Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay
landmarks.summary: The Pantanal is a natural region encompassing the world's largest tropical wetland area, and the world's largest flooded grasslands. It is located mostly within the Brazilian state of Mato Grosso do Sul, but it extends into Mato Grosso and portions of Bolivia and Paraguay.

landmarks.name: Lake Kivu
landmarks.description: Meromictic lake in the East African Rift valley
landmarks.summary: Lake Kivu is one of the African Great Lakes. It lies on the border between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, and is in the Albertine Rift, the western branch of the East African Rift. Lake Kivu empties into the Ruzizi River, which flows southwards into Lake Tanganyika.

landmarks.summary: Rothenburg ob der Tauber is a town in the district of Ansbach of Mittelfranken, in the Franconia region of Bavaria, Germany. It is best known for its well-preserved medieval old town, a destination for tourists from around the world. It is part of the popular Romantic Road through southern Germany.

landmarks.summary: Ushuaia is the capital of Tierra del Fuego, Antártida e Islas del Atlántico Sur Province, Argentina. With a population of 89,606 and a location below the 54th parallel south latitude, Ushuaia claims the title of the world's southernmost city.

landmarks.summary: The Pyramid of Djoser, also known as the Step Pyramid of Djoser or Step Pyramid of Horus Netjerikhet, is an archaeological site in the Saqqara necropolis, Egypt, northwest of the ruins of Memphis. landmarks.summary: Belém Tower, officially the Tower of Saint Vincent, is a 16th-century fortification located in Lisbon, Portugal, which served as a point of embarkation and disembarkation for Portuguese explorers and as a ceremonial gateway to Lisbon. The tower symbolizes Portugal's maritime and colonial power in early modern Europe.

landmarks.summary: Hohenzollern Castle is the ancestral seat of the formerly imperial House of Hohenzollern. landmarks.description: Natural site in Denizli Province in southwestern Turkey
landmarks.summary: Pamukkale, meaning "cotton castle" in Turkish, is a natural site in Denizli Province in southwestern Turkey. The area is famous for a carbonate mineral left by the flowing of thermal spring water. It is located in Turkey's Inner Aegean region, in the River Menderes valley, which has a temperate climate for most of the year.

landmarks.name: Checkpoint Charlie
landmarks.description: Crossing point in the Berlin Wall
landmarks.summary: Checkpoint Charlie was the Western Bloc's name for the best-known Berlin Wall crossing point between East Berlin and West Berlin during the Cold War (1947–1991), becoming a symbol of the Cold War, representing the separation of East and West.

landmarks.name: Devil's Island
landmarks.description: Prison of Cayenne in French Guiana
landmarks.summary: The penal colony of Cayenne, commonly known as Devil's Island, was a French penal colony that operated for 100 years, from 1852 to 1952, and officially closed in 1953, in the Salvation Islands of French Guiana.

landmarks.name: Eiger

landmarks.summary: The Eiger is a 3,967-metre (13,015 ft) mountain of the Bernese Alps, overlooking Grindelwald and Lauterbrunnen in the Bernese Oberland of Switzerland, just north of the main watershed and border with Valais.

landmarks.description: Capital city in Chuquisaca Department, Bolivia
landmarks.summary: Sucre, officially La Ilustre y Heroica Sucre is the de jure capital city of Bolivia, the capital of the Chuquisaca Department and the sixth most populous city in Bolivia. Located in the south-central part of the country, Sucre lies at an elevation of 2,790 m (9,150 ft), making it the second-highest capital city in the world after Quito.

landmarks.summary: Bouvet Island is an uninhabited subantarctic volcanic island and dependency of Norway. A protected nature reserve situated in the South Atlantic Ocean at the southern end of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, it is the world's most remote island.

landmarks.name: Leshan Giant Buddha
landmarks.summary: The Leshan Giant Buddha is a 71-meter (233 ft) tall stone statue, built between 712 and 804 AD. It is carved out of a cliff face of Cretaceous red bed sandstones that lies at the confluence of the Min River and Dadu River in the southern part of Sichuan Province in China, near the city of Leshan.

landmarks.name: Park Güell
landmarks.description: Public park system in Barcelona, Spain
landmarks.summary: Park Güell is a complex of parks and gardens in Barcelona with architectural elements, located in the La Salut neighborhood of the Gràcia district in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain. It is situated on the southern slope of the Turó del Carmel hill, part of the Collserola mountain range, overlooking the city.

landmarks.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
landmarks.summary: Gyeongbokgung is a former royal palace in Seoul, South Korea. Established in 1395, it was the first royal palace of the Joseon dynasty, and is now one of the most significant tourist attractions in the country.

landmarks.name: Khajuraho
landmarks.description: Historic temples in Madhya Pradesh, India
landmarks.summary: The Khajuraho Group of Monuments are a group of Hindu and Digambara Jain temples in Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh, India. 6 mi) from Rajnagar. The temples are famous for their Nagara-style architectural symbolism and a few erotic sculptures.

landmarks.name: Pont du Gard
landmarks.summary: The Pont du Gard is an ancient Roman aqueduct bridge built in the first century AD to carry water over 50 km (31 mi) to the Roman colony of Nemausus (Nîmes). It crosses the river Gardon near the town of Vers-Pont-du-Gard in southern France. The Pont du Gard is one of the best preserved Roman aqueduct bridges.

landmarks.name: Vatican Museums
landmarks.summary: The Vatican Museums are the public museums of the Vatican City. They display works from the immense collection amassed by the Catholic Church and the papacy throughout the centuries, including several of the best-known Roman sculptures and most important masterpieces of Renaissance art in the world.

credit.title: File:Room XII (17th century) of the Pinacoteca Vaticana.jpg
credit.author: Petar Milošević

landmarks.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
landmarks.description: Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto, Japan
landmarks.summary: Kinkaku-ji , officially named Rokuon-ji , is a Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto, Japan and a tourist attraction. It is designated as a World Heritage Site, a National Special Historic Site, a National Special Landscape, and one of the 17 Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto. 5 μm gold leaf.

landmarks.name: Diocletian's Palace
landmarks.summary: Diocletian's Palace is an ancient Roman palace and fortress complex in Split, Croatia. It was built at the end of the third century AD by the Roman Emperor Diocletian as his retirement residence. About half of the complex was for Diocletian's personal use, with the rest housing the military garrison.

landmarks.name: Mahabodhi Temple
landmarks.description: Buddhist temple in Bodh Gaya, India
landmarks.summary: The Mahabodhi Temple or the Mahābodhi Mahāvihāra, is a restored Buddhist temple in Bodh Gaya, Bihar, India, marking the location where the Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment, according to the Buddhist faith.

landmarks.name: Mount Roraima
landmarks.description: Mountain in Brazil, Guyana and Venezuela
landmarks.summary: Mount Roraima is the highest of the Pacaraima chain of tepuis or plateaux in South America. It is located at the junction of Brazil, Guyana and Venezuela.

landmarks.name: Cozumel
landmarks.summary: Cozumel is an island and municipality in the Caribbean Sea off the eastern coast of Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula, opposite Playa del Carmen. It is separated from the mainland by the Cozumel Channel and is close to the Yucatán Channel. The municipality is part of the state of Quintana Roo, Mexico.
